name: level2-playthrough-win
description: Level 2 (Grumpstone Ridge) playthrough: 3 surveys, a freight warehouse, four far-flung living quarters, five blast-plan cycles and five contract acceptances on a funded ($3,000,000) mine that stays solvent and revolt-free throughout. #1431 (rebuilt after #1313 froze the mine at level end): the original $150,000 opening went bankrupt at tick 176 and the file played on over a lost game; the quarters (placed far from every blast pattern so no blast destroys them) keep wellBeing up and the run ends as a real win: `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` is locked on a fresh campaign, so the file runs on the new_game world and closes with `campaign complete level:grumpstone_ridge`, which activates level 2 and ends it 'completed' with profit at the $250,000 threshold. Drillers and blasters die in blasts, so each later pattern re-hires and re-equips a crew and rig.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true added -- cash:150000 sits on this new_game, not on the campaign start below, because that command fails outright (grumpstone_ridge is tier-2, locked on a fresh campaign, Finding #59), so it never replaces this state and a cash: on it would be discarded with the rest of the command. staffed:true hires and equips its own free crew before any assertion here: employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1), #2 blaster, #3-5 drivers, vehicle #1 drill_rig, #2 debris_hauler, #3 rock_digger, #4 rock_fragmenter -- free, not deducted from cash, which is why employeeCount is already 5 here instead of 0. All four vehicles come unmanned (driverId: null); vehicle driver 1 1 immediately below crews the free rig with the free driller, since drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action and nothing drills without a driver aboard. The extra $100,000 over the sandbox default is what the three-vehicle fleet at step 36 needs, same as before -- but see the pattern-1 drill-wait step further down for what that budget can no longer survive once drilling takes hundreds of ticks instead of zero.

#1379: the default site policy (shift_8h, threshold 60) is always in force and would force-rest the crew. This file is not about rest, so continuous mode with the lowest rest threshold (0) neutralizes it and keeps the pre-#1379 no-policy timings.

#953: a blasted bench is no longer terrain a worker walks off -- its face is a six-voxel drop, and pathfinding now refuses that step instead of letting haulers stroll over the edge. Access to the pit floor is a dug ramp, exactly as gameplay-navmesh describes it, so this level digs one from the rim at (24,14) down into the block it is about to blast, before the blast rather than after (cash is still positive here, and the excavation crew has the three tick-150 steps below to finish it). Without it every haul_debris action queued by the first blast targets a cell no employee can reach: traced flat at one stored fragment for 2400 ticks, and the four contract-deliver steps below all refuse with 'Not enough stored material'. #1151: origin moved from (24,12) to (24,6) and depth set explicitly to 7 (was the unspecified default 8) -- length 13 now satisfies length >= ceil(depth * 1.8), keeping every per-column step within NAV_MAX_SLOPE_RATIO, while floor((length-1)/length * depth) = floor(12/13*7) = 6 keeps the ramp's actual deepest carved column at the same six-voxel drop the surrounding blast (drill depth:6) and this description already assume -- the old length:7/depth:8 pairing reached that same 6 via floor(6/7*8). The corridor's own footprint roughly doubles in length, so its total excavated volume is larger than before; if a future scenario run finds the ramp not fully dug by the point haul_debris needs it, widen the tick-150 budget below rather than re-shorten the ramp back below the new slope minimum.

VehicleContinuity.ts releases a follow-up action's own pre-existing vehicle reservation before transferring the just-finished vehicle's reservation onto it, instead of leaving both reserved) -- each shifts exactly which vehicle drives which trip and when across this file's own vehicle-scarce fleet, the same cash/ecology/nuisance-only-recalibration shape #1002/#953 above already document for an identical class of dispatch-timing change. deathCount, employeeCount, activeContractCount, surveyCount, wellBeing, and safety all reproduce unchanged -- direct-verified via `npx tsx scripts/scenario-test.ts --scenario level2-playthrough-win --report-drift`, command mode; the new numbers are exact and reproducible run to run. #953: ecology 50 -> 48.94 and nuisance 50 -> 47.35 are the ramp dug at step 41 showing up in the scores — excavating one is real earthmoving, and this level's first blast now happens on a site that already has a haul road cut into it. #1002 (starvation-override vehicle-reservation release + distance-based vehicle tie-break): ecology corrected again, 48.93 -> 48.97, and nuisance 47.325 -> 47.425 -- a starvation dismount now also frees any taskQueue-held vehicle reservation back to the pool, and a tied vehicle claim is now broken by distance to the claiming employee instead of lowest id, both of which shift exactly which vehicle drives which trip and when; that nudges the earthmoving accounted for by the time of this checkpoint. deathCount, employeeCount, activeContractCount, surveyCount, wellBeing, and safety all reproduce unchanged -- direct-verified via `npx tsx scripts/scenario-test.ts --scenario level2-playthrough-win`, command mode (clean, uncontended run — an earlier measurement taken while `npm run test`'s full suite ran concurrently on the same 2-core sandbox produced a stale 47.325 for this one CPU-contended step; every clean rerun since, standalone and in the full `npm run scenarios` batch, reproduces 47.425 exactly); the new number is exact and reproducible run to run. #1107 (merge of main into #1089's branch): ecology corrected again, 48.87 -> 48.9, nuisance 47.175 -> 47.25, and cash -637,450.897 -> -636,943.897 -- tickCollapse now releases a vehicle reservation held by an action still sitting unboarded in a collapsing employee's taskQueue (#1096, PR #1107), and tickEmployees no longer re-reserves it for a collapsing employee on the next tick, so a vehicle returns to the pool for the length of every collapse instead of idling reserved. steps.description: #553/#593: wellBeing craters to 0 -- 2 deaths at blast 1 (down from the pre-#593 file's 4, see the blast step above), plus every surviving employee's morale sits at 0 (sandbox-measured `employee list`, no living_quarters anywhere in this file to recover it). #1270 (resolved): `relocateFootprintOccupants` (`BuildingTaskHelpers.ts`) now sweeps `state.vehicles.vehicles` the same way it already swept `state.employees.employees`, so vehicle #3 (the idle `rock_digger` parked at (6,2)) is relocated off the `freight_warehouse` footprint the instant that build order is placed, instead of being stranded there. The `build_ramp` job's driver can reach and claim it normally, employee #4 is dispatched into blast 1's radius as they were pre-#1200, and every figure below is re-measured against the fixed dispatch (ground truth captured via `--report-drift`), not hand-derived.

issue #585 (command-mode-only): raised 6 -> 45 (confirmed via direct trace, createGameEngine + runCommand replay) -- with the freight_warehouse now built (see the vehicle-buy-assign step's own note), storedMassKg still traces flat at 0.0 through the original 6 ticks: the debris_hauler auto-claimed by driver #3 has to walk from its own spawn tile to vehicle #2, drive it roughly 20+ tiles out to the nearest on-ground fragment, load, then drive back to the depot -- none of which lands inside 6 ticks. Traced in 2-tick increments: the first fragment (a mixed-material haul, not pure ore) delivers around tick+16, a second around tick+24, after which delivery plateaus (a separate, deeper HaulDispatch limitation -- the hauler's second dispatch stalls; #552's own known gap) at storedMassKg ~2160kg / collectedOre.rustite ~425kg, comfortably past both group deliveries below. 45 was chosen (not the smaller values that also clear that plateau) because this file's pattern-2 charge order (charge hole:*, well below) is timing-sensitive to the exact absolute tick this step lands on -- smaller offsets (16, 24, 40) left one hole still mid-load when blast 2's own fixed-length charge-wait ran out ("Invalid plan: H11/H15: Charge still loading"), a downstream regression direct trace caught and is not this step's own concern to explain further than to say 45 was verified clean through blast 2 and beyond. #953: raised 45 -> 70 -- the climb-limit gate makes the hauler's ordinary route to its nearest on-ground fragment cost more ticks whenever the route crosses a bench-level boundary (ramp-based multi-level pathing instead of a straight walk); direct trace (npx tsx scripts/run-all-scenarios.ts level2-playthrough-win) confirmed 70 clears the original storedMassKg-plateau this step exists to reach (~795kg stored by this point, comfortably above every downstream contract amount). #973: a separate, pre-existing Logistics.ts issue (consumeStoredOre's rubble branch deleted an oversized stored fragment's entire surplus rather than partially consuming it) meant a contract-deliver step later in this file could still be refused depending on which single fragment happened to be first in storage -- unrelated to this step's own tick value, not fixed by raising it further (traced identical at tick 70/100/250). Fixed in #973 via splitStoredFragmentMass, unrelated to this step's own tick value. #674: interaction mode ran its own, unchanged `tick 6` here -- a 39-tick gap that put every later step of the two modes on different absolute ticks and was the whole of this file own command/interaction divergence (first state-dump difference of the run, tickCount 598 vs 559, everything before it byte-identical). Realigned to this step's own declared `tick` value.
